Smart50 alumni secures major partnership with Poland’s Xtreme Brands Australian fitness franchise Strong Pilates has entered into a major partnership with Poland’s largest wellness franchise operator Xtreme Brands. Morganne Kopittke Aug 5, 2026 3 min read Share 0 Prefer SmartCompany STRONG Pilates founders Michael Ramsey and Mark Armstrong. Source: supplied Australian fitness franchise Strong Pilates has entered into a major partnership with Poland’s largest wellness franchise operator Xtreme Brands, as the fast-growing company looks to add central and eastern Europe to its growing portfolio. Under the new master franchise agreement, Strong Pilates will expand first into Poland and the Czech Republic, taking its global footprint to 16 countries including Australia, the US, New Zealand, Canada, the UK, Ireland, Japan, Singapore, Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia, South Korea, Dubai and Bahrain. Related Article Block Placeholder Article ID: 339914 2026 Smart50 Awards open for entries, biggest prize in event’s history on offer Eloise Keating Strong Pilates, which was co-founded in Melbourne in 2019 by former F45 franchisees Michael Ramsey and Mark Armstrong, is known for its blend of pilates, cardio and strength training via the Rowformer and Bikeformer machines. The fitness franchise has grown from strength to strength over the past year, with the company securing 10th place on the Smart50 list at the 2025 Smart50 Awards , up from 21 on the 2024 list . Over the past 12 months Strong Pilates has recorded US$75 million ($106 million) in group revenue and has more than 125 operating studios globally, with a further 200 studios confirmed to open soon. It has 46 employees across the board, with two thirds based in Australia, alongside teams in the US, UK, and Canada. A Strong Pilates studio. Source: supplied Strong Pilates gears up for further international expansion Strong Pilates co-CEO Michael Ramsey said the new partnership with Xtreme Brands will usher in an “exciting time” for the fast-growing business. “The partnership will allow us to accelerate our growth and build credibility in new markets,” he told SmartCompany . Ramsey said Strong Pilates is the first external brand to join Xtreme Brands’ existing portfolio, which includes 189 fitness gyms. “Xtreme Brands is aiming for 750 operating locations by 2030, with many of these being Strong Pilates studios,” he added. Xtreme Fitness Gyms CEO James Cotton said the partnership also marks a significant milestone for the group, as it welcomes its first international brand to its network amid rapid expansion plans. “Strong Pilates is a proven international concept that responds to growing demand for training that combines pilates, strength and cardio,” he said. This will involve comprehensive onboarding, training, education and engaging fitness communities in new markets. When asked about the future, Ramsey confirmed Strong Pilates has exciting growth plans underway across Europe and the Middle East, while also continuing to evolve its programming, equipment and technology to continue to serve its members. Ramsey added Australia is the company’s largest and most established market and it is committed to further growing its presence across the country. “With 66 studios nationwide, and more than 50% owned by multi-site operators, our network demonstrates the strength, scalability and long-term commitment of our franchise community,” he said. Strong Pilates made the Smart50 list of Australia’s fastest growing SMEs in 2024 and 2025. Photograph: Brendan Smialowski/AFP/Getty Images James Comey Justice department charges ex-FBI director James Comey for third time Comey, an outspoken critic of Donald Trump, accused of leaking information related to US national defense Sam Levine Mon 26 Oct 2026 18.17 EDT Last modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 18.18 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The justice department charged former FBI director James Comey on Monday with two counts of leaking information related to national defense, the third time the Trump administration has filed criminal charges against one of Donald Trump’s most despised foes. The charges, filed in federal court in Washington DC, provide few details about what Comey is alleged to have leaked. The government alleges that the former FBI director leaked the information in 2016 and conspired with an unnamed person to give the information to a national news outlet. Patrick Fitzgerald, Comey’s attorney, said the charges were related to a 5 October 2016 New York Times article that had already been investigated by prosecutors. The case was filed through a criminal maneuver known as an “information” – meaning it was not approved by a grand jury. While prosecutors will eventually have to have the charges approved by a grand jury, filing the charges through an information appears to have been an effort to quickly get the criminal charges in against Comey before the 10-year statute of limitations expires. “Ten years after the article was published, the government filed an ‘information’ against Mr Comey that was not approved by a judge nor issued by a grand jury. It purports to charge Mr Comey with crimes he did not commit,” Fitzgerald said in a statement. In a court filing unsealed on Monday , Comey’s lawyers argued the indictment should be dismissed because the statute of limitations had expired and it had been twice investigated and determined no charges should be filed. They also argued that the law required an indictment, not an information, within the 10-year statute of limitations. Trump fired Comey in 2017 as he worked on an investigation into whether Trump allies colluded with Russia during the 2016 presidential election. The former FBI director has since become an outspoken critic of the president. Last year, the justice department charged Comey with lying to Congress, but the charges were thrown out after a judge found the prosecutor handling the case, a White House ally installed to bring the case, was unlawfully appointed. Earlier this year, the justice department filed charges against Comey in federal court in North Carolina for posting a picture of a formation of seashells spelling out “8647” – which for some people is a shorthand way of saying get rid of Trump. Legal experts have said that case is thin. “Well, they’re back again. It would almost be funny if wasn’t such an appalling abuse of the Department of Justice. One that we cannot become numb to,” Comey said in a video posted online. Czech Republic: Meerkats and cheetah cubs play with Halloween pumpkins Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 30 October 2026 - 14:50 GMT+1 Halloween has arrived at Prague Zoo, where meerkats are exploring pumpkins stuffed with worms and cheetah cubs are discovering seasonal toys. Four days of activities will bring treats to 14 animal species. … More Meerkats searched carved pumpkins for worms on Friday, 30 October , while cheetah cubs played with their own Halloween surprise and a caracal was filmed licking another. Keepers provided extra treats as pumpkins of different shapes, sizes and colours were distributed around the zoo, where 14 animal species are expected to join the celebrations. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT The Halloween activities are also designed to encourage natural behaviour through animal enrichment , a technique that introduces new objects, food and challenges into an animal's environment. For the meerkats, searching for worms inside hollowed-out pumpkins turns feeding time into an opportunity to explore and forage. Cheetah and caracal cubs are being introduced to pumpkins for the first time, giving them something unfamiliar to investigate and play with. By combining seasonal decorations with stimulating activities, Prague Zoo is using the autumn holiday to provide its animals with new experiences while offering visitors a glimpse of their curiosity and playful behaviour.
